- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >2.5x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 2.5x prior 7-day average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for low sentiment + upward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply 10–15% upward bias for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average.
- For long-term (15–30 day) forecasts, model often overreacts to sentiment spikes; apply 20–30% downward correction if sentiment >0.75 and price >3.0.
